title: Compact pushout presentations survive arrow retracts
statement: Fix a universe $\mathcal U$; small means $\mathcal U$-small. Let $\tau\in\mathcal U$ be an uncountable regular cardinal, where regular means that a union of fewer than $\tau$ sets each of cardinality less than $\tau$ has cardinality less than $\tau$. A category is $\tau$-filtered if every diagram with fewer than $\tau$ morphisms has a cocone. An object is $\tau$-presentable if its Hom functor preserves small $\tau$-filtered colimits. Let $\mathcal A$ be an ordinary category with small Hom sets and all small colimits [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit], with a small family of $\tau$-presentable objects such that every object is the colimit of a small $\tau$-filtered diagram of objects of this family. A pushout means a colimit of a span. Let $u:P\to Q$ be a morphism between $\tau$-presentable objects. Let $g:V\to W$ be its pushout along some $P\to V$. Suppose $g':V'\to W'$ is a retract of $g$ in the arrow category: there are commuting squares $s:g'\to g$ and $r:g\to g'$ with $rs=1_{g'}$ (the arrow category has arrows as objects and commuting squares as morphisms). There exist $\tau$-presentable objects $P',Q'$, a map $u':P'\to Q'$ and a map $P'\to V'$ such that $g'$ is a pushout of $u'$ along that map and $u'$ belongs to the weakly saturated closure of $\{u\}$. Here the weakly saturated closure is the smallest arrow class containing $u$ and all isomorphisms and closed under pushouts, small continuous transfinite compositions and arrow retracts; continuous means that each nonzero limit stage is the colimit of its predecessors. No presentability of $V,V',W,W'$ is assumed.

source.place: HTT Lemma A.1.5.10, printed pp. 805-806; read online 2026-10-17, not archived in literature/. No Stacks tag states this result.

proof.text: Write the components of the arrow retraction as $s_0:V'\to V$, $r_0:V\to V'$, $s_1:W'\to W$, $r_1:W\to W'$. Form $Y=V'\amalg_V W$ using $r_0$ and $g$, with maps $h:V'\to Y$ and $k:W\to Y$. The pushout universal property [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit] identifies $h$ with the pushout of $u$ along $P\to V\xrightarrow{r_0}V'$. The maps $g'$ and $r_1$ induce $b:Y\to W'$, since $g'r_0=r_1g$. Put $c=ks_1:W'\to Y$. Then $bc=r_1s_1=1$, $cg'=kgs_0=hr_0s_0=h$, and $bh=g'$. Hence $e=cb:Y\to Y$ is idempotent and $eh=h$. From now on write $X=V'$, $a:P\to X$ for the new attaching map, so $Y=X\amalg_P Q$, and retain the specified split image $X\xrightarrow{g'}W'$ of $h$. This changes neither $u$ nor the desired conclusion.

source.place: HTT A.1.5.10, first paragraph of proof: reduction to a common source

proof.text: By the hypothesis on $\mathcal A$, choose a small $\tau$-filtered diagram of objects $X_i$ of the given family with colimit $X$; each $X_i$ is $\tau$-presentable. Apply [lem-coef-cardinal-filtered-poset-reindex] to replace the index category by a small $\tau$-filtered poset $I$, preserving the specified cocone $x_i:X_i\to X$. Since $P$ is $\tau$-presentable, $\operatorname{Hom}(P,X)=\operatorname{colim}_i\operatorname{Hom}(P,X_i)$; the representative clause of [lem-weil-pbc-filtered-colimit-sets-elementwise] gives $i_0$ and $a_{i_0}:P\to X_{i_0}$ representing $a$. Restrict to $I_{\geq i_0}$ and put $a_i=t_{i_0i}a_{i_0}$. This tail remains small and $\tau$-filtered: any fewer than $\tau$ indices together with $i_0$ have an upper bound. It still presents $X$: a cocone on the tail extends to $i$ by choosing $j\geq i,i_0$ and composing $X_i\to X_j$ with its component; a common upper bound proves independence and compatibility. Thus there is a compatible attaching map $P\to X_i$ at every stage.

source.place: HTT A.1.5.10, second paragraph: filtered presentation under the compact source

proof.text: Set $Y_i=X_i\amalg_P Q$, with structure maps $h_i:X_i\to Y_i$, $d_i:Q\to Y_i$, transitions $v_{ij}:Y_i\to Y_j$ and maps $\lambda_i:Y_i\to Y$. The cocone $(Y,(\lambda_i))$ is colimiting: a compatible family $Y_i\to Z$ is precisely a compatible family $X_i\to Z$ and a single $Q\to Z$ agreeing on $P$. Indeed all the $Q$ components agree because any two indices have a common upper bound. Such data are precisely a map $X\to Z$ and a map $Q\to Z$ agreeing on $P$, hence precisely a map $Y\to Z$ by [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]. Each $Y_i$ is $\tau$-presentable by [lem-coef-ordinary-small-colimit-presentable], applied to the finite span $X_i\leftarrow P\to Q$. No presentability of $X$ or $Y$ is asserted.

source.place: HTT A.1.5.10, second paragraph: pushout-stage presentation and presentability

proof.text: Let $d:Q\to Y$ be the pushout map. By $\tau$-presentability of $Q$ and the representative clause of [lem-weil-pbc-filtered-colimit-sets-elementwise], the map $ed:Q\to Y$ factors as $\lambda_i j$ with $j:Q\to Y_i$. The two maps $ju,h_ia_i:P\to Y_i$ become equal in $Y$, because $\lambda_i ju=edu=eha=ha=\lambda_i h_ia_i$. Apply the same node's eventual-equality clause to the diagram $k\mapsto\operatorname{Hom}(P,Y_k)$, using $\tau$-presentability of $P$, to obtain $k\geq i$ with $v_{ik}ju=v_{ik}h_ia_i=h_kt_{ik}a_i=h_ka_k$, where $t_{ik}:X_i\to X_k$ is the transition. Set $j_k=v_{ik}j$; then $\lambda_kj_k=ed$ and $j_ku=h_ka_k$. Replace $i,j$ by $k,j_k$. The pushout property now defines $e_i:Y_i\to Y_i$ with $e_ih_i=h_i$ and $e_id_i=j$. On the two pushout legs one checks $\lambda_i e_i=e\lambda_i$.

source.place: HTT A.1.5.10, second paragraph: factor the endomorphism and enforce the attaching equation

proof.text: For $k\geq i$, define $e_k:Y_k\to Y_k$ by $e_kh_k=h_k$ and $e_kd_k=v_{ik}j$. Its attaching equation follows from that of $j$, and checking on the legs gives $e_kv_{ik}=v_{ik}e_i$ and $\lambda_ke_k=e\lambda_k$. The maps $e_ij,j:Q\to Y_i$ have equal composites to $Y$, since $\lambda_i e_i j=e\lambda_i j=e^2d=ed=\lambda_i j$. By $\tau$-presentability of $Q$ and the eventual-equality clause of [lem-weil-pbc-filtered-colimit-sets-elementwise], choose $k\geq i$ with $v_{ik}e_ij=v_{ik}j$. It follows that $e_k^2d_k=e_kv_{ik}j=v_{ik}e_ij=v_{ik}j=e_kd_k$, while $e_k^2h_k=h_k=e_kh_k$. The pushout property therefore gives $e_k^2=e_k$. Relabel this stage $i$. This explicitly supplies the source's 'enlarging once more': it does not assume that the transition maps are monomorphisms.

source.place: HTT A.1.5.10, end of printed p. 805 and beginning of p. 806: descend idempotence

proof.text: Split the idempotent without assuming idempotent completeness: take its coequalizer $q:Y_i\to Q'$ of $e_i$ and $1_{Y_i}$ [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]. Since $e_i^2=e_i$, there is $t:Q'\to Y_i$ with $tq=e_i$. Also $qtq=qe_i=q$; coequalizer maps are epimorphisms directly by uniqueness in their universal property, so $qt=1$. The object $Q'$ is $\tau$-presentable by [lem-coef-ordinary-small-colimit-presentable], since this coequalizer is a finite colimit of copies of the $\tau$-presentable object $Y_i$. Put $P'=X_i$ and $u'=qh_i:P'\to Q'$. The equalities $tu'=e_ih_i=h_i$ and $qt=1$ exhibit $u'$ as an arrow retract of $h_i$, with identity maps on $X_i$. As $h_i$ is a pushout of $u$, closure under pushouts and arrow retracts puts $u'$ in the weakly saturated closure of $\{u\}$.

source.place: HTT A.1.5.10, printed p. 806: split the finite-stage idempotent and obtain presentability and weak saturation

proof.text: The desired square has top $u':X_i\to Q'$, left $x_i:X_i\to X=V'$, bottom $g':X\to W'$, and right $\delta=b\lambda_it:Q'\to W'$. It commutes: $\delta q=b\lambda_i e_i=b e\lambda_i=b\lambda_i$, hence $\delta u'=b\lambda_i h_i=g'x_i$. Verify its pushout property explicitly [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]. Given $z:X\to Z$ and $w:Q'\to Z$ with $zx_i=wu'$, the pushout square $X_i\to Y_i$, $X\to Y$ gives a unique $F:Y\to Z$ with $Fh=z$ and $F\lambda_i=wq$. To check this pushout assertion directly, maps $z:X\to Z$ and $f_i:Y_i\to Z$ with $zx_i=f_ih_i$ give $z$ and $f_id_i:Q\to Z$ agreeing on $P$, since $za=zx_ia_i=f_ih_ia_i=f_id_iu$. The pushout $Y=X\amalg_P Q$ supplies a unique $F$ with $Fh=z$ and $Fd=f_id_i$; its restrictions to the two legs of $Y_i$ give $F\lambda_i=f_i$. Conversely any $F$ gives this compatible pair, proving the assertion. Apply it with $f_i=wq$. Now $Fe=F$: their restrictions to $X$ agree as $eh=h$, and their restrictions to $Y_i$ agree as $e\lambda_i=\lambda_ie_i$ and $qe_i=q$. Thus $Fc:W'\to Z$ satisfies $(Fc)g'=z$ and $(Fc)\delta=Fcb\lambda_it=Fe\lambda_it=wqt=w$. For uniqueness, if $l:W'\to Z$ satisfies these two equations, then $lb:Y\to Z$ has restrictions $z$ on $X$ and $wq$ on $Y_i$ (use $b\lambda_i=\delta q$), so $lb=F$ and $l=lbc=Fc$. This proves the required pushout, and completes all clauses with the original source $V'$.
